facts.statement: The only known specimen of Equijubus was discovered in the summer of 2000 by a Chinese-American expedition in Gansu Province, China.
facts.quote: The type (and only known) specimen was found in the summer of 2000 by a Chinese-American expedition in the Mazong (= "horse mane") Shan area of China's Gansu Province.

facts.statement: The species Equijubus normani was first named and described in a dissertation by You Hailu in 2002.
facts.quote: In 2002 You Hialu in a dissertation named and described the species Equijubus normani.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V12534 includes a complete skull with attached lower jaws and nine neck, sixteen back, and six pelvic vertebrae.
facts.quote: The type specimen or holotype, IVPP V12534, consists of a complete skull with articulated (attached) lower jaws, plus associated incomplete postcrania: nine cervical (neck), sixteen dorsal (back), and six sacral (pelvic) vertebrae.

facts.statement: Equijubus was a herbivorous dinosaur living during the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) in northwestern China.
facts.quote: Equijubus (; Mǎzōng meaning "horse mane" after the area Mǎzōng Mountain 马鬃山 in which it was found), is a genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) of northwestern China.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Equijubus reached a length of seven meters and a weight of 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 2010 estimated the length at seven metres, the weight at 2.5 tonnes.

facts.statement: The skull of Equijubus is approximately 65 centimeters long and has a somewhat rectangular shape.
facts.quote: El cráneo, de unos 65 centímetros de largo, tiene una forma algo rectangular.

facts.statement: Equijubus lacked the typical eyebrow bone that shades the eye socket, a feature found in most related species.
facts.quote: La cuenca ocular carece del sombreado típico de un hueso de ceja que la mayoría de los familiares tienen.

facts.statement: Grass microfossils found in an Equijubus specimen in 2018 were the oldest known grass fossils and suggest the dinosaur may have been a grazer.
facts.quote: Wu, You & Li (2018) described grass microfossils extracted from a specimen of Equijubus normani, which at the time of their description were the oldest known grass fossils, and might be the oldest known evidence of a dinosaur feeding on grasses, implying that it was most likely a grazer.

facts.statement: Equijubus is classified as a basal hadrosauroid, though some analyses suggest it may be a non-hadrosauroid iguanodont.
facts.quote: Equijubus was described as a basal hadrosauroid dinosaur, although it may turn out to be a non-hadrosauroid iguanodont.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Equijubus belongs to the Hadrosauroidea or represents a long branch originating from Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los análisis posteriores a menudo tuvieron un resultado diferente donde Equijubus es un hadrosauroide, pero proviene de una larga serie de ramas a partir de Iguanodon.

facts.statement: Equijubus lived approximately 100 million years ago in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: hace aproximadamente entre 100 millones de años en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Equijubus lived between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Equijubus is classified within the suborder Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: infraordo: Iguanodontia

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Equijubus contained twenty-three tooth positions.
facts.quote: El maxilar tiene veintitrés posiciones de dientes.

facts.statement: There is a clear gap of about six centimeters between the upper row of teeth and the upper beak in Equijubus.
facts.quote: Hay una separación clara, de unos seis centímetros, entre la fila superior de dientes y el pico superior.

facts.statement: Equijubus had tightly packed teeth in a dental battery with a second generation of replacement supports present.
facts.quote: Los dientes están apretados en la batería dental; una segunda generación de soportes de reemplazo está actualmente presente.

facts.statement: Equijubus possessed six fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Hay seis vértebras sacras fusionadas.

facts.statement: The generic name Equijubus is derived from the Chinese meaning of Mazong Shan, which translates to "horse mane".
facts.quote: La etimología del nombre genérico proviene de región de Mazong Shan, que significa "crin de caballo" en chino, en el área de la Provincia de Gansu.

facts.statement: The specific epithet "normani" honors the British paleontologist David B. Norman.
facts.quote: El epíteto de la especie, "normani", es en honor al paleontólogo inglés David B. Norman.

facts.statement: Original phylogenetic analysis suggested Equijubus was the most basal known member of Hadrosauroidea, the sister group to a monophyletic Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: Los descriptores llevaron a cabo un cladograma del análisis filogenético con el resultado de que Equijubus era el miembro más básico conocido de la Hadrosauroidea, un grupo que sería el grupo hermano de un Iguanodontidae monofilético.
